Hero.description: I build modern websites as well as web and mobile applications using React, Next.js and TypeScript. I focus on clear interfaces, responsiveness and attention to detail, using AI as support in my daily work. Check out my projects and see how they work in practice

AboutMe.title: About me
AboutMe.intro: My name is Patryk Jastrzębowski. I’m 20 years old and a Fullstack Developer with a degree in IT technician studies. In my free time, I focus on programming and creating modern websites as well as web and mobile applications. I mostly work with Next.js, React, TypeScript and JavaScript, styling interfaces with TailwindCSS. I use Git and GitHub for version control. I also use AI tools to support the process of building websites and applications, but not as a replacement for independent thinking
AboutMe.moreInfo: I am well organised, committed to my tasks and effective at managing my time. I approach projects with full focus. I want to grow alongside more experienced developers and have a real impact on the product. I combine theory with practice by regularly building new projects and publishing them on my GitHub profile. I approach programming with passion and consistency

responsive.title: Responsive design
responsive.text: CSS Grid, Flexbox and breakpoints. Websites adapted for desktops, tablets and phones, with attention to readability and comfortable use on every screen. Consistent appearance and intuitive navigation regardless of device size

uiux.title: UI/UX design
uiux.text: Modern visuals, 3D elements and projects created with AI support. Attention to colours, typography and element states, from hover and focus to errors and loading. Interfaces that are visually pleasing and comfortable to use on any device

cleanCode.title: Clean code
cleanCode.text: Readable and well-organised code that other developers can understand. Clear naming and a division into small parts, each with a specific purpose. Components and functions that can be reused, easily improved and extended without unnecessary code duplication

ai.title: Working with AI tools
ai.text: AI as support, not a replacement for thinking. Help with finding bugs, understanding code and generating interface ideas. Reviewing and adapting suggestions instead of copying ready-made answers without reflection. Experimenting with tools and looking for new ways to improve my workflow

database.title: Databases
database.text: MySQL, PostgreSQL and data management: creating, reading, updating and deleting records. User authentication and roles that define who can view or modify specific information. Additional RLS policies ensure that users can access only the data intended for them

components.title: Reusable components
components.text: Buttons, forms and cards built as reusable components. Configuration through props and consistent visual variants instead of duplicating code. Changes made in one place make it easier to develop and maintain the entire application

Projects.title: My projects
Projects.problemDescription: Create an e-commerce application that combines convenient product browsing with simple catalogue management. It was also important to separate customer and administrator access and adapt the interface to different screen sizes
Projects.solutionDescription: A Next.js and Supabase application with search, sorting, a shopping cart and interactive 3D models. The admin panel allows product and image management, while authentication, user roles and RLS policies control data access
Projects.effectDescription: A demonstration store with a responsive interface and catalogue management panel. Users can browse products, view specifications and add items to the cart, while administrators can update the offer without editing code

mindhealth.description: An application that supports mental wellbeing. Users can record how they feel each day, track it in a calendar, build daily streaks and use mindfulness exercises, a thought journal and an AI chatbot offering support

travelDreams.description: A mobile application for saving places you want to visit. Users can mark dream locations on a map, add photos and short descriptions, and browse or remove saved points to create a personal travel wishlist

earth3d.description: An interactive landing page about Earth. Its main feature is a 3D model of the planet that reacts to scrolling with position, rotation and zoom animations, complemented by sections with information about Earth

kindle.description: A web application for collecting Kindle highlights in one place. After importing notes, it automatically detects the book title, author and highlights. Users can search and sort books and quotes

pinkyPromise.description: A responsive website for a private nail stylist. It presents services, prices, duration, a portfolio of work and information about the artist, while making it easy to contact and book an appointment through a consistent pink visual identity

flora.description: A responsive landing page about plants and flowers. It features an animated background, eye-catching cards that react to cursor movement and a modern, readable layout that makes browsing content easier

CaseStudy.title: Case study
CaseStudy.description: A demonstration e-commerce application inspired by Apple products. It combines a product catalogue, interactive 3D models and a shopping cart with an offer management panel. Users can browse specifications and add products to the cart, while administrators can add and update the catalogue. It is an educational project and is not a real store or Apple’s official website

catalog.title: Catalogue and cart
catalog.text: Browse products by category, search and sort them. Detailed specifications and a cart that updates immediately after changes

models.title: 3D models
models.text: Interactive models of selected products that let users view a device from different angles and examine its appearance

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.text: Add, edit and remove products without changing code. Upload images with automatic cropping and complete product specifications

auth.title: Accounts and permissions
auth.text: Registration and sign-in with Supabase Auth. Separate access for users and administrators, with RLS policies controlling data access

CaseStudy.goalText: The goal was to create a demonstration store that combines convenient product browsing with offer management. The project includes both the user-facing part and an admin panel with a catalogue, cart, accounts and access control
CaseStudy.interfaceText: The category-based catalogue complements search, sorting and detailed specifications. Interactive 3D models let users view selected devices from different angles. The experience is completed by a responsive layout, loading states and hover effects
CaseStudy.databaseText: The project was built with Next.js, Supabase and shadcn/ui components. Data is divided into four main tables: categories, products, related products and user roles. This structure connects the catalogue with the information needed to manage the offer and permissions
CaseStudy.adminText: The admin panel supports product, image and specification management. Forms are validated on the server, and deleting a product requires confirmation. User roles restrict access to the panel, while RLS policies control access at the database level
CaseStudy.resultText: The result is a demonstration e-commerce application with a user-facing part and administrator tools. It combines the interface, authentication, database and catalogue management in one application. It does not process real sales, its purpose is to demonstrate the described features in practice

details.title: Attention to detail
details.text: I care not only about appearance, but also about how comfortable an application is to use. A clear layout, responsiveness and well-designed button and form states are part of a finished project

code.title: Code
code.text: I write code that other developers can easily understand and extend. I focus on clear naming, organised structure and reusable components that make changes easier without repeating code

ai.title: Using AI wisely
ai.text: I use AI to better understand code, find bugs and explore interface ideas. I do not copy answers without thinking, I analyse suggestions and adapt them to the needs of the project

growth.title: Growth through practice
growth.text: I regularly build projects and publish them on GitHub. I work consistently, engage with tasks and want to learn from more experienced developers while having a real impact on the product
